name: Microsoft Corporation

thesisState.summary: Deep Dive v1.2, user valuation model v1.2 and thesis memo v1.1 integrated. Current framing: high-quality enterprise software/cloud compounder with AI upside, but valuation depends primarily on AI capex normalization and FCF conversion.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Evidence that AI/cloud capex remains structurally high without corresponding durable Azure/Copilot monetization.
Material deterioration in FCF conversion, ROIC or operating margins after the AI infrastructure buildout.
Multiple compression because AI turns MSFT into a materially more capital-intensive hard-asset business rather than a software/cloud compounder.
Competitive/regulatory pressure that weakens Microsoft Cloud, Office/Copilot or enterprise distribution advantage.

businessSnapshot.description: Global software, cloud, productivity, operating systems, gaming and enterprise infrastructure company.
businessSnapshot.cycleExposure: Moderate enterprise IT/cloud cycle exposure; AI infrastructure investment cycle is key current variable.

keyDrivers: Enterprise software switching costs and distribution strength across Office, Windows, Azure, GitHub and security.
Azure scale, growth and margin quality as the core cloud value driver.
Copilot/AI monetization converting infrastructure spend into higher ARPU and retention.
Operating margin resilience while absorbing AI infrastructure, D&A and R&D intensity.
FCF recovery as capex/revenue normalizes after the FY26-FY27 investment cycle.
keyRisks: AI capex remains structurally high and depresses FCF conversion.
Multiple compression if AI economics look more like capital-intensive infrastructure than software.
Azure growth or Copilot monetization disappoints relative to the capex base.
Cloud competition and pricing pressure from AWS, Google and other infrastructure providers.
Regulatory/antitrust constraints around bundling, platform power and AI partnerships.
watchMetrics: Azure growth and AI contribution commentary
Copilot adoption, pricing, retention and ARPU evidence
FCF margin / FCFF revenue conversion versus model assumptions
Operating margin by segment and Intelligent Cloud margin quality
Commercial RPO / bookings and duration commentary
openQuestions: Can terminal capex/revenue normalize toward the model’s ~15% assumption without impairing AI/cloud growth?
How much of AI capex is offensive ROI-generating capacity versus defensive participation cost?
What valuation multiple is justified if AI structurally lowers FCF conversion versus the historical software profile?
At what price range does MSFT compensate enough for capex and multiple-compression risk?
